Class 10 Mathematics: monthly board-revision
cycle - teacher guide
Virat International School • HBSE 2026-27 • Months planned: November 2026 (transition) and December 2026 • Status: DRAFT -
awaiting teacher approval
1. How the monthly cycle works
Week  Whole school  This subject (group A)
Week 1  Group A subjects: full-syllabus revision (concepts,  Full-syllabus pass
important topics, textbook-based questions)
Week 2  Group B subjects: full-syllabus revision with weak areas,  Application + answer writing (cumulative: all of Week 1
application and previous-year-style questions  reappears)
Week 3  All subjects: intensive consolidation - active recall, timed  Timed consolidation of every unit, then a mini-mock
practice, competency/case-based questions, numericals,
error correction
Last week  Subject-wise pre-board in the HBSE pattern, time and  Pre-board 2 (Dec); Pre-board 1 (Nov)
marking scheme
  Every chapter/unit of the 2026-27 syllabus is revised in Weeks 1-3 of every month (coverage tables below - tick each row
when done).
  Cumulative recall: every period opens with 5 minutes on chapters revised earlier, so nothing is left behind.
  Question mix in every practice set: textbook-based, previous-year board questions (from official BSEH papers the school
holds), sample-paper-style, competency/case-based and one higher-order item.
  High-weightage units get the application periods first (table 2), but no unit is skipped.
  Pre-board results drive the next month: use the gap-analysis rubric (folder 05) to choose the units for the next month's gap-
work periods and the students for small-group support.
2. Unit weightage (HBSE 2026-27) and revision targets
Unit / section  Marks  Chapters / items
Unit I Number Systems  6  1
Unit II Algebra  20  4
Unit IV Geometry  15  2
Unit III Coordinate Geometry  6  1
Unit V Trigonometry  12  2
Unit VI Mensuration  10  2
Unit VII Statistics and Probability  11  2
Targets (proposed - teacher to confirm):
  End of Week 1/2: every chapter ticked in the coverage table; every student has the revision sheet for each chapter and has
attempted its questions.
  End of Week 3: each unit practised at least once under time; each student keeps an error log; class average on timed sets at
least 60% in December and 70% in January.
  Pre-board: every student attempts every section within time; after the pre-board, each student has three named target
areas for next month.
3. Answer-writing practice for this subject
Board paper: 80 marks in 3 hours → about 2.2 minutes per mark. Time every drill on this basis (a 5-mark answer ≈ 11 min).
Question type (pre-board design)  Count × marks
Objective  20 × 1
VSA  5 × 2
SA  6 × 3
LA  4 × 5
Case  3 × 4
Show every step: board marking awards marks for method. Practise one 4-5 mark problem under time in every application
period. Draw neat figures for geometry and heights-and-distances.
4. Period routines (35 minutes)
  Full-syllabus pass: 5 min cumulative recall (chapters listed) → 15 min key concepts / formula / summary map (students pre-
read the revision sheet at home) → 12 min textbook- and board-type questions on these chapters → 3 min exit check (1
question per chapter).
  Application + answer writing: 5 min recall → 22 min timed answer writing on the listed unit (previous-year-style and
competency/case-based questions; HOTS item for the top group) → 8 min marking against the scheme, students correct in
a different colour and log errors.
  Gap work + answer writing: 5 min recall → 22 min timed answer writing on the listed unit, prioritising the weakest units
from the last pre-board → 8 min marking against the scheme and error log.
  Timed consolidation: 25 min timed mixed set (objective + short + one long/case/numerical/map item as per the board
design) on the listed units → 10 min error correction against the marking scheme; each student updates the error log.
  Mini-mock + error correction: 30 min timed section in the exact board format across all units → 5 min debrief: time
management, presentation, the three most common errors; final checklist for the pre-board.
5. November 2026 (transition cycle): period-by-period plan
Week 1: Mon 02 Nov - Fri 06 Nov • Week 2: Thu 12 Nov - Tue 17 Nov • Week 3: Wed 18 Nov - Fri 20 Nov • Pre-board 1: Sat 21
Nov - Sat 28 Nov. Short cycle: Diwali break 7-11 Nov; W3 assumes Classes 10/12 do not sit UT-3 (18-25 Nov) because Pre-board
1 replaces it (approval AP09). Dates are PROPOSED until approved.

  The course structure lists 'Production Function and Costs' as 18 marks and gives 'Profit Maximisation & Supply Curve' as a

  Percentage-method numerical value of elasticity is used (Q4, Q25 OR, Q31); the syllabus lists price elasticity and total
expenditure method, so the definition of elasticity is assumed to be as per the NCERT textbook.
